With pytest 5.x, we can dynamically add an xfail to a test `request` object using `request.node.add_marker(mark)` (see example below). In 5.x this treated the failing test like a a test marked statically with an `xfail`. With 6.0.0rc0 it raises.

payload.result: Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

structured_output.command:
cd /testbed && /opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"
src = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:
        # A xfail mark might have been applied dynamically during the test
        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the
        # evaluation is up to date before deciding how to report.
        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")
EOF

Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"

old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:
        # A xfail mark might have been applied dynamically during the test
        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the
        # evaluation is up to date before deciding how to report.
        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")

Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"
src = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:
        # A xfail mark might have been applied dynamically during the test
        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the
        # evaluation is up to date before deciding how to report.
        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")

Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"
src = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:
        # A xfail mark might have been applied dynamically during the test
        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the
        # evaluation is up to date before deciding how to report.
        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")

In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"
src = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:
        # A xfail mark might have been applied dynamically during the test
        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the
        # evaluation is up to date before deciding how to report.
        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")

In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io

    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

import io
p = "src/_pytest/skipping.py"

old = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

new = '''    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)
    if not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed is None:

        # itself (e.g. using ``request.node.add_marker``), so make sure the

        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key
'''
assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))

Now I understand the regression. In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

In pytest 6, `xfail` marks are evaluated once in `pytest_runtest_setup`/`pytest_runtest_call` and cached in `item._store[xfailed_key]`; a marker added dynamically during the test call is never re-evaluated, so `pytest_runtest_makereport` sees `None`. Let me apply the fix.

    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, None)

        item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    # unittest special case, see setting of unexpectedsuccess_key

assert src.count(old) == 1
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src.replace(old, new))
